- codex:codex-rescue: Proactively use when Claude Code is stuck, wants a second implementation or diagnosis pass, needs a deeper root-cause investigation, or should hand a substantial coding task to Codex through the shared runtime (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

Spawned by do-arc's eval step and the eval-arc skill; never recomputes a deterministic signal. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Bash)

- zeroh-roadmap:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, pattern adherence, and business rule correctness using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Edit, Write, Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch, TodoWrite, LSP)

- zeroh-roadmap:intent-validator: Independent intent judge — drives the real shipped flow at one acceptance criterion's tier, captures concrete evidence, scores fulfilled intent against a rubric, and returns a typed IntentVerdict. Spawned by validate-arc, one per criterion; never grades work it built. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch, TodoWrite)

- zeroh-roadmap:phase-executor: Runs do-phase for ONE phase end-to-end inside an arc and returns a structured PhaseExecutionResult. Spawned by the do-arc orchestrator; never user-invoked. (Tools: All tools)

- zeroh-roadmap:quality-pass: One-shot end-of-phase quality sweep — the merged architect-critique + simplifier pass. Additive half fixes shortcuts, hardcodes, cross-task patterns, and neighborhood issues in touched files; subtractive half deletes dead scaffolding, speculative abstractions, and noise. Auto-fixes in scope; hard-stops on multi-repo / scoped-out / product / speculative. Runs once per phase (reviewScope full only), before the code-review loop. - lead-sentinel: Operate as the fleet's lead sentinel — the voice-connected manager session that dispatches goals to worker sessions, monitors their state, reviews their work, and reports to the owner. Use when this session is the Viky voice brain or the owner asks for fleet status, dispatch, nudge, review of other sessions' work, or what the fleet should work on next.

- zeroh-roadmap:arc-sweep: Pre-merge sweep for a built arc: dispose every accumulated compromise (reusing release-sweep's debt vocabulary) and run one whole-arc software-architect review against the arc's singleSeams + designRefs, then report merge-readiness.
- zeroh-roadmap:audit-roadmap: Read-only structural audit across roadmap state and the vendored schema (17 checks). Reports findings only — never fixes.
- zeroh-roadmap:do-arc: Execute a whole arc end to end: launch one per-plane workflow at a time, own the halts it hands back, sweep + validate in-session, and land via the CLI.
- zeroh-roadmap:do-phase: Execute a roadmap phase task-by-task with enforced sequential discipline: one task = one commit + a transparencyReport, then the kind-selected gate.
- zeroh-roadmap:eval-arc: Score a landed arc across the seven ratified dimensions — code confidence, verified-vs-intent, standards adherence, doc brevity, composability/testability, speed, plan quality — into a typed, dated ArcEvalReport ratcheted against a rolling baseline. The standalone door onto do-arc's Step 9, for arcs that landed without it.
- zeroh-roadmap:full-code-review: Whole-codebase pre-release audit. Parallel agents cover security, dead code, duplication, performance, architecture, edge cases, data flow, and domain-critical calculations; findings become a release verdict (any critical blocks), a remediation phase, and a review-record round. Use for "full code review", "pre-release audit", a pre-prod checkup on worry areas, or before merge-to-main/prod deploy. Not this skill: diff/phase review (code-review); a consumer's own release-review supersedes this.
- zeroh-roadmap:handoff: Routes unfinished session context into durable roadmap artifacts, leaving only justified residue for a fresh session. Use for requests to hand off work, hand off to a fresh session, continue in a new session, write a context file, or produce a one-line prompt.
- zeroh-roadmap:plan-arc: Plan a whole arc (a named, contiguous block of phases shipped as one unit): author the Arc entity, resolve the design-first gate WITH the user (reuse / new design / inherited ratified prototype / recorded skip), plan every member phase against that design, review each independently, queue one arc tier. Triggers: 'plan arc', '/plan-arc', 'create arc', 'new arc'. Not this skill: one standalone phase (plan-phase) or executing an existing arc (do-arc).
- zeroh-roadmap:plan-phase: Create a new roadmap phase. Use when user says: create phase, plan phase, add to roadmap, new phase, add feature, create task. Reads the code first, pre-makes every decision, rehearses verifies in both directions, then writes and commits a .phase.ts file. Not this skill: planning a multi-phase arc (plan-arc, which loops plan-phase per member) or queueing/auditing an existing phase (review-phase owns the queue).
- zeroh-roadmap:release-sweep: Review and resolve outstanding debts for a release version, then optionally archive the version's done phases. Run before every minor/major; optional before patches. Patch releases are never blocked on debts; archive is.
- zeroh-roadmap:review-phase: Independently verify a roadmap phase or whole arc against the real code: backlog phases get a plan-quality review that repairs the plan and queues it; done/in-progress phases get a report-only post-execution audit. Trigger: 'review phase N', '/review-phase N', 'verify/audit phase N', 'review arc <ID>'; also the mandatory pre-queue pass after plan-phase and the spawned judge step in plan-arc. Not for general diff/PR review or bug hunting - that is a plain diff review (the code-reviewer agent).

- zeroh-roadmap:using-zeroh-roadmap: ALWAYS ACTIVE. Phase-driven development plugin. MUST be used when user says: create phase, plan phase, do phase, roadmap, review phase, code review, what's next, arc, sweep, backlog. Routes ALL development task requests through the phase system.

When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. | --- | --- |
| init / new repo / scaffold | greenfield-init |

{"route":"greenfield-init|brownfield-audit|stack-decision","evidence":["<repository-relative-path>"]}

Define `<repository-relative-path>` as an inspected marker path. If inspection cannot resolve the repository root, STOP with `route: unresolved` and the attempted path; this STOP is honor-system.

- Delegate Blade tokens, themes, and branded design work to `zeroh-design`; record only its pointers.
- Keep the trigger map in this router. Treat both ownership rules as honor-system; each routed skill names this router as the reverse boundary.

# Brownfield marker table

Inspect every row. Evidence supports classification but absence never proves a stack.

| Artefact | Evidence glob | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Package managers | `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `package-lock.json`, `uv.lock`, `pubspec.yaml`, `gradlew` | Present files identify installed package tooling; conflicting locks are partial or stale evidence. |
| Framework files | `next.config.*`, `app.json`, `android/`, `pubspec.yaml`, `vite.config.*` | Framework-owned configuration supports a candidate stack that stack-decision must confirm. |
| Monorepo tools | `nx.json`, `turbo.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `lerna.json` | Existing workspace orchestration is preserved and linked. |
| Docs | `README.md`, `docs/**/*.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` | Existing fact homes are inventoried before proposing a missing index or canon. |
| Harness files | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.cursor/rules/**`, `.codex/**`, `opencode.json` | Apply the harness inventory and generated-block preservation contract. |
| Roadmap config | `roadmap/roadmap.config.json`, `roadmap/phases/`, `docs/roadmap/roadmap.config.json`, `docs/roadmap/phases/`, the explicit `ROADMAP_ROOT` path | Existing roadmap configuration is merged, never reinitialized. |
| Superpowers directory | `.superpowers/`, `docs/superpowers/` | Existing planning artifacts are linked rather than duplicated. |
| Design-system files | `components.json`, `**/components.json`, `tokens/**`, `**/*theme*`, `docs/**/*design*` | Registries and token homes are evidence for design reconciliation, not permission to invent values. |

## Canonical roadmap discovery
Resolve the consumer Git toplevel first. Use `roadmapRoot(consumerRoot)` from the
installed zeroh-roadmap `cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs`; resolve that module from the
installed plugin, never from an assumed consumer-relative plugin directory.
Pass the consumer root explicitly, retain `ROADMAP_ROOT`, and inspect
`<resolved root>/roadmap.config.json`. Do not infer absence from a top-level glob.
A marked root without a config is partial: STOP for an approved recovery proposal,
not fresh initialization. Ambiguous roots STOP with the resolver's remedy; an
